title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous pages. X/S is a smooth morphism, and ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. V is a rank-3 bundle with an orthogonal (SO(3)≅PGL(2)) structure, so V behaves like Sym^2 of a rank-2 bundle. It carries the flag Fil_1 = Ω ⊂ Fil_2 = L ⊂ V, with gr = (Ω, O_X, Ω^{-1}) and V/L ≅ Ω^{-1}. Equivalently there is a conic bundle P/X with a section σ.

Results already obtained. A connection c on V compatible with the structure satisfies Griffiths transversality c(Fil_i) ⊂ Fil_{i-1}(V⊗ω). Its graded pieces are O-linear maps c_{1,2}: Ω→ω and c_{2,3}: O→Ω^{-1}⊗ω, and they satisfy c_{1,2} = -2c_{2,3}. The connections form a torsor under V⊗ω. Pushing forward along V⊗ω→Ω^{-1}⊗ω gives the map ϖ_0. Fixing ϖ_0 = i reduces the structure group to L⊗ω, and pushing further to ω gives a torsor under ω.

Restricting c to Ω gives c_Ω: Ω → L⊗ω. This is a first-order differential operator with c_Ω(fθ) - f c_Ω(θ) = θ⊗df in Ω⊗ω ⊂ L⊗ω (property **). Its composite Ω→L⊗ω→ω is linear and equal to -2i (property *).

This page.
(1) Giving such a c_Ω amounts to a reduction of the structure group of Conn_i to Ω⊗ω-type subtorsors. Independently of i, giving a c_Ω satisfying (*) linear and (**) amounts to a reduction of the structure group of Conn to Ω⊗ω.
(2) Grothendieck then specialises to the case where the composite Ω→L⊗ω→ω (= -2i) is an isomorphism. This is the 'transverse' or 'nowhere stationary' case named on the next page, i.e. the oper condition.
(3) Claim: assuming ω is invertible (relative curves), the triple (V, L, c_Ω), or equivalently (L⊃Ω, c_Ω), is determined by X/S up to unique isomorphism. Explicitly, L ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, so L⊗ω ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω), and c_Ω is the universal first-order operator d^1_{X/S,ω}: ω → P^1(ω).

Why the claim holds. By the universal property of principal parts, c_Ω factors uniquely as u∘d^1 with u: P^1(ω)→L⊗ω linear. Both P^1(ω) and L⊗ω are extensions of ω by ω^{⊗2}. Property (**) forces u to be the identity on the subobject ω^{⊗2} (after identifying Ω≅ω via i). Property (*) forces u to induce an isomorphism on the quotient. By the five lemma u is an isomorphism, and it is unique.

Outcome. The PGL_2-oper (indigenous bundle) has a canonical underlying filtered bundle given by jets: L is the canonical extension 0→ω→L→O→0 of class the Atiyah/Kodaira-Spencer type class. The next page goes on to define transverse connections as a torsor under L⊗ω, i.e. the affine space of projective structures. The purpose, in the volume on Gauss-Manin and Cartier, is presumably to study uniformising/indigenous connections on curves, possibly together with p-curvature.
errors: The transversality condition uses the factor -2 (c_{1,2} = -2c_{2,3}). Requiring Ω→ω to be an isomorphism therefore needs 2 invertible on S; in characteristic 2 such a structure is never transverse. This hypothesis is not stated on the page.

There is a normalisation mismatch. The canonical d^1: ω→P^1(ω) composed with P^1(ω)→ω is the identity, whereas the composite here is -2i. So the identification Ω≅ω must be rescaled (by -2) for c_Ω to literally equal d^1. This is harmless but left implicit.
'ℳ⊗ω' in the first lines is probably a slip or misreading for Ω⊗ω or L⊗ω, given the two parallel statements.

ideas.what: Graded/transversal components of a filtered SO(3)-connection, with transversality ('nowhere stationary') meaning the second fundamental form is an isomorphism
The underlying filtered bundle of a transverse structure is canonically given by first-order principal parts: L ≅ P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, with c_Ω = d^1
ideas.modern_name: Jet-bundle description of the oper bundle (V ≅ J^2 of ω^{-1}, rigidity of the oper filtration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in projective-structure / oper theory (Gunning, Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki for the p-adic case)

ideas.what: Torsor descriptions of connection spaces and their successive structure-group reductions (V⊗ω → L⊗ω → ω)
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of opers/projective structures modelled on quadratic differentials

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops the algebraic theory of PGL_2-opers (indigenous bundles) over a general base X/S, explicitly in terms of principal parts. This sits inside a dossier devoted to Gauss-Manin connections and the Cartier operation (c. 1972-81). That suggests an early algebraic, relative and possibly characteristic-p treatment, predating the Beilinson–Drinfeld oper formalism and Mochizuki's p-adic indigenous bundles.
missed.quote: (V, L, c_Ω) ... est défini à isom unique près par X/S ... comme L ≃ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1} ... c_Ω : Ω ≃ ω → L⊗ω ≃ P^1_{X/S}(ω)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the relative, jet-theoretic formulation of opers. If later pages link this to p-curvature or the Cartier operator, it would anticipate dormant opers (Mochizuki, Joshi–Pauly, Wakabayashi).

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is the standard rigidity of the oper filtration via jets, and is routine for specialists. What is notable is the historical context: an algebraic, relative treatment of indigenous bundles by Grothendieck within a Cartier/Gauss-Manin dossier is not, to my knowledge, documented in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'On s'intéresse au cas où ℰ et c_Ω est tel que' should probably read 'où i et c_Ω sont tels que'.
'ou ce qui revient au =' means 'ou ce qui revient au même'.
'Conn_i ℰ à ℳ⊗ω' is likely 'Conn_i à L⊗ω' or 'Ω⊗ω'.
The last line 'induit autre que d^1_{X/S,ω}' is probably 'induit par l'opérateur d^1_{X/S,ω}' (i.e. c_Ω is the canonical d^1).
'(et avant tout ω = Ω^1_{X/S} est inversible)' probably reads '(et pourvu que ω = Ω^1_{X/S} soit inversible)'.
